#### 1. immunodeficiency 36 with lymphoproliferation  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.422)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9013404, Reactome:R-HSA-9013408, Reactome:R-HSA-9013423)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in PIK3R1 —DISRUPTS→ PIK3R1 (HGNC:9473); PIK3R1 (HGNC:9473) —DECREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-425557); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-425557) —LEADS_TO→ Ventricular dysfunction (HP:0001648); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-425557) —LEADS_TO→ Lymphoproliferation (HP:0002771). Pathogenic variants in PIK3R1 lead to loss-of-function, which in turn dysregulates the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway. This dysregulation can manifest as ventricular dysfunction in ARVD10 and lymphoproliferation in immunodeficiency 36.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a pathogenic variant in PIK3R1 that leads to a gain-of-function effect in either disease, or the identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways for each disease. _(variant: rs74355374 (common variant in PIK3R1, allele frequency > 1%))_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the PI3K-Akt pathway could offer therapeutic avenues for both arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia 10 and immunodeficiency 36 with lymphoproliferation, although disease-specific modulation would be crucial.

#### 2. familial caudal dysgenesis  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.398)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9013404, Reactome:R-HSA-9013408, Reactome:R-HSA-9013423)

**Proposed mechanism:** DSG2 (HGNC:2910) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosomal adhesion (GO:0007156); Desmosomal adhesion (GO:0007156) —LEADS_TO→ Planar cell polarity pathway (WP:WP420); VANGL1 (HGNC:12163) —DISRUPTS→ Planar cell polarity pathway (WP:WP420); Planar cell polarity pathway (WP:WP420) —LEADS_TO→ Arrhythmia (HP:0011692); Planar cell polarity pathway (WP:WP420) —LEADS_TO→ Caudal regression sequence (HP:0003304). Mutations in DSG2 disrupt desmosomal adhesion, which in turn impacts the planar cell polarity pathway, leading to arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia. Similarly, mutations in VANGL1 directly disrupt the planar cell polarity pathway, causing familial caudal dysgenesis. The convergence is on the planar cell polarity pathway, essential for both cardiac and embryonic development.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in DSG2 are found to cause familial caudal dysgenesis or mutations in VANGL1 are found to cause arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia 10, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, if genetic studies reveal distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways downstream of DSG2 and VANGL1 that do not converge at the level of the planar cell polarity pathway, this would also falsify the hypothesis. _(variant: The presence of common variants (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) in either DSG2 or VANGL1 associated with either phenotype would challenge the rare variant hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of DSG2 and VANGL1 in the planar cell polarity pathway could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both cardiac arrhythmias and developmental disorders affecting posterior structures. Modulating this pathway might offer a unified approach to treating conditions arising from disruptions in cell adhesion and tissue polarity.
